title: Reviewer initial and finalize endpoints omit training_scope.resolve('review') and training_scope.sid_allowed(va_sid)
description: In app/routes/api/reviewing.py, all read and allocation endpoints (get_allocation, allocate, release_allocation, stats, projects, available, history) call training_scope.resolve('review'), and allocate additionally checks training_scope.sid_allowed(va_sid). Likewise, all coder assessment write endpoints in app/routes/api/coding.py (initial, finalize, not_codeable) and the shared DORIS clinical context in app/routes/api/doris_clinical.py (_clinical_context) call training_scope.resolve(...) and verify training_scope.sid_allowed(va_sid). However, POST /api/v1/reviewing/finalize/<va_sid> (finalize, lines 219-282) and POST /api/v1/reviewing/initial/<va_sid> (initial, lines 285-343) in app/routes/api/reviewing.py omit both training_scope.resolve('review') and training_scope.sid_allowed(va_sid), and submit_reviewer_final_cod (lines 533-540) and submit_reviewer_initial_cod (lines 808-815) in app/services/reviewer_coding_service.py do not check VaAllocations.va_allocation_training.is_(training_scope.on_training_side()). Although require_reviewer_access still enforces Action.REVIEW grant reach on va_sid, requests to these two endpoints ignore ?training=1, skip training_demo_service.may_use_area(current_user.user_id, 'review') when ?training=1 is passed, and allow cross-boundary reviewer assessment writes between real work (training=0 or absent, where training_scope.current() defaults to EXCLUDE) and the training project (TRN01, ?training=1).
claimed_root_cause: app/routes/api/reviewing.py#finalize (lines 219-282) and app/routes/api/reviewing.py#initial (lines 285-343) do not call training_scope.resolve('review') or check training_scope.sid_allowed(va_sid) before invoking submit_reviewer_final_cod and submit_reviewer_initial_cod in app/services/reviewer_coding_service.py, and those service functions do not filter the active VaAllocations lookup by VaAllocations.va_allocation_training.is_(training_scope.on_training_side()).

trace.description: POST /api/v1/reviewing/finalize/<va_sid> accepts a reviewer final COD request with va_sid and optional ?training= query parameter without calling training_scope.resolve('review') or training_scope.sid_allowed(va_sid).
finalize delegates directly to submit_reviewer_final_cod(current_user, va_sid, ...) while the request scope remains at the default training_scope.EXCLUDE regardless of ?training=.
submit_reviewer_final_cod queries VaAllocations for an active reviewing allocation on va_sid without filtering on VaAllocations.va_allocation_training.is_(training_scope.on_training_side()).

POST /api/v1/reviewing/initial/<va_sid> similarly accepts a reviewer Step 1 COD request without calling training_scope.resolve('review') or training_scope.sid_allowed(va_sid) before calling submit_reviewer_initial_cod at line 320.
submit_reviewer_initial_cod queries VaAllocations for an active reviewing allocation on va_sid without filtering on VaAllocations.va_allocation_training.is_(training_scope.on_training_side()).

create_reviewer_final_assessment (and create_reviewer_initial_assessment at line 901) persists the reviewer assessment and transitions the submission workflow state across the real/training scope boundary.

evidence.description: allocate(va_sid) in the same blueprint calls training_scope.resolve('review') and checks training_scope.sid_allowed(va_sid) at line 117, returning 409 not_available across the training/real line.
finalize(va_sid) starts with get_project_for_submission(va_sid) and never calls training_scope.resolve('review') or training_scope.sid_allowed(va_sid).
initial(va_sid) starts with get_project_for_submission(va_sid) and never calls training_scope.resolve('review') or training_scope.sid_allowed(va_sid).

By contrast, coder initial(va_sid) (lines 538-543) and finalize(va_sid) (lines 584-589) call training_scope.resolve('coding') and refuse cross-scope writes with 409 not_available via training_scope.sid_allowed(va_sid).

_clinical_context calls training_scope.resolve('review' if role == 'reviewer' else 'coding'), checks training_scope.sid_allowed(va_sid) at line 123, and filters VaAllocations by VaAllocations.va_allocation_training == training_scope.on_training_side() at line 148.
training_scope.current() defaults to EXCLUDE on every request unless resolve() is called, and sid_allowed(va_sid) at line 178 only runs when explicitly invoked.

blockers: OS-enforced sandbox execution (no external network, empty allowlisted environment, read-only target and tool mounts, scratch-only writes, and explicit resource and wall-clock limits) is unavailable on this VM to run the Flask test client against a disposable test database.

validation_plan.local: Inside an approved sandbox with an isolated disposable PostgreSQL test database, run a non-destructive pytest case extending ReviewingScopeTests in tests/test_training_scope.py: allocate both REAL_SID (without ?training=1) and self.training_sid (with ?training=1), then send POST /api/v1/reviewing/initial/<training_sid> and POST /api/v1/reviewing/finalize/<training_sid> without ?training=1, and POST /api/v1/reviewing/initial/<REAL_SID>?training=1 and POST /api/v1/reviewing/finalize/<REAL_SID>?training=1. Observe that they are not rejected with 409 not_available (unlike the corresponding /api/v1/coding/initial and /api/v1/coding/finalize routes in test_recode_and_code_now_are_refused_across_the_line).

title: Missing training_scope enforcement and client-controlled mode gate in POST /api/v1/va/<va_sid>/social-autopsy and POST /api/v1/va/<va_sid>/narrative-qa
description: POST /api/v1/va/<va_sid>/social-autopsy (save_social_autopsy in app/routes/api/so.py:54-239) and POST /api/v1/va/<va_sid>/narrative-qa (save_narrative_qa in app/routes/api/nqa.py:53-212) do not call training_scope.resolve(...) or training_scope.sid_allowed(va_sid) and do not filter VaAllocations by va_allocation_training. In addition, save_social_autopsy and save_narrative_qa branch between reviewer access checks and coder access checks using client-supplied va_actiontype while persisting VaSocialAutopsyAnalysis and VaNarrativeAssessment rows keyed by (va_sid, user_id, payload_version_id), and require_coding_access (app/utils/va_permission/va_permission_11_require_coding_access.py:34-37) skips the VaAllocations lookup when an admin sends va_actiontype='vademo_start_coding' on a demo-training submission.
claimed_root_cause: save_social_autopsy (app/routes/api/so.py:56-95) and save_narrative_qa (app/routes/api/nqa.py:55-89) omit training_scope.resolve, training_scope.sid_allowed(va_sid), and VaAllocations.va_allocation_training filters, and select between reviewer authorization/feature gates and coder authorization/feature gates from client-supplied va_actiontype while writing to per-(va_sid, user_id, payload_version_id) artifact tables and allowing admin vademo_start_coding requests on demo submissions without an allocation.

trace.description: Authenticated POST /api/v1/va/<va_sid>/social-autopsy handler reads JSON body and client-supplied va_actiontype.

Computes is_reviewer_session from va_actiontype in {'vastartreviewing', 'varesumereviewing'} and dispatches to either the reviewer permission/allocation check (lines 71-82) or require_coding_access(va_sid) (line 84).

Verifies coding access: allows admin demo saves when va_actiontype == 'vademo_start_coding' and is_demo_training_submission(va_sid) is true (lines 34-37), otherwise requires can(current_user, Action.CODE, va_sid) and an active VaAllocation.coding row for (current_user.user_id, va_sid) (lines 51-69).
Acquires a row lock on the submission and re-verifies the caller's active reviewing or coding allocation before mutating artifacts.
Creates or updates the active VaSocialAutopsyAnalysis record for (va_sid, current_user.user_id, active_payload_version.payload_version_id).

evidence.description: Module contract specifies that training_scope partitions list, count, and allocation-acquisition endpoints between the TRN01 training project and real projects based on ?training=.
Coding allocations set va_allocation_training = training_scope.is_training_sid(va_sid) from the submission's project at allocation creation time.
Reviewer allocations set va_allocation_training = training_scope.is_training_sid(va_sid) from the submission's project at allocation creation time.

Reviewer branch enforces both live grant check can(current_user, Action.REVIEW, va_sid) and an active VaAllocation.reviewing row for (current_user.user_id, va_sid), then re-confirms under lock at lines 153-155.

Reviewer branch in save_narrative_qa likewise enforces can(current_user, Action.REVIEW, va_sid) and an active VaAllocation.reviewing row for (current_user.user_id, va_sid), re-confirmed under lock at lines 124-126.

Coder branch enforces can(current_user, Action.CODE, va_sid) and an active VaAllocation.coding row for (current_user.user_id, va_sid), and is re-invoked under submission lock at app/routes/api/so.py:157-158 and app/routes/api/nqa.py:128-129.
Finalizing coder COD deactivates the coder's VaAllocation.coding row before the submission transitions to reviewer_eligible.
A reviewer allocation can only be created when the submission workflow state is WORKFLOW_REVIEWER_ELIGIBLE, preventing concurrent active coding and reviewing allocations on the same va_sid.

social_autopsy_enabled(project, 'vareview') requires both project.social_autopsy_enabled and project.reviewer_social_autopsy_enabled, so reviewer social autopsy is never enabled when project.social_autopsy_enabled is false.

Unit test test_admin_demo_save_on_a_demo_submission_needs_no_allocation explicitly verifies as intended behavior that an admin sending va_actiontype='vademo_start_coding' on a demo_training_enabled project can save without an allocation row.

reason: Source code refutes all three parts of the candidate: (1) training_scope separates the TRN01 training project from real projects on list, count, and allocation-acquisition routes (app/services/training_scope.py:5-18; app/routes/api/coding.py:179,193; app/routes/api/reviewing.py:116-118). Once a submission is allocated, va_sid belongs to a single project and VaAllocations.va_allocation_training is deterministically derived from training_scope.is_training_sid(va_sid) (app/services/coder_workflow_service.py:885; app/services/reviewer_coding_service.py:442). Because save_social_autopsy and save_narrative_qa require both a live grant check via can(current_user, Action.CODE or Action.REVIEW, va_sid) and an active VaAllocations row matching that exact va_sid (app/routes/api/so.py:71-86,152-161; app/routes/api/nqa.py:73-88,123-132), omitting ?training= or VaAllocations.va_allocation_training does not allow cross-scope access or saves on unallocated submissions (and the Expo client intentionally calls these per-submission endpoints without ?training= in mobile/digitva-collect/src/workspace/api.ts:247-248). (2) Although va_actiontype selects between the reviewer and coder branches, each branch independently enforces both its action grant (Action.REVIEW vs Action.CODE) and an active allocation of the matching type (VaAllocation.reviewing vs VaAllocation.coding) on va_sid before and after locking the submission. A submission cannot simultaneously have active coding and reviewing allocations because coder finalization deactivates the coding allocation (app/services/coder_cod_service.py:999) before reviewer allocation is permitted in WORKFLOW_REVIEWER_ELIGIBLE (app/services/reviewer_coding_service.py:412), so a caller cannot flip va_actiontype to bypass reviewer_social_autopsy_enabled or coder_social_autopsy_enabled during an active session. (3) Allowing an admin with va_actiontype='vademo_start_coding' on a demo_training_enabled submission to save without an allocation in require_coding_access (app/utils/va_permission/va_permission_11_require_coding_access.py:34-37) is documented and tested design for ephemeral admin demo testing (tests/routes/test_narrative_qa.py:374-385), and any resulting row is restricted to demo projects, scoped to the admin's own user_id, and stamped with demo_expires_at (app/routes/api/so.py:180,198; app/routes/api/nqa.py:157,181).

title: Unbounded remark length and missing route-level body cap in POST /api/v1/va/<va_sid>/social-autopsy allow multi-megabyte database and workspace payload amplification
description: Unlike PUT /api/v1/va/<va_sid>/note (app/routes/api/va_case.py:898-958, which enforces a 64 KB Content-Length cap, rejects NUL characters, and enforces a 20,000-character content limit), POST /api/v1/coding/finalize/<va_sid> (app/routes/api/coding.py:442,611, which enforces a 4,000-character _FREE_TEXT_CAP on remark), and /api/v1/doris-clinical/* (app/routes/api/doris_clinical.py:212-216, which enforces a 32 KB Content-Length cap), POST /api/v1/va/<va_sid>/social-autopsy (save_social_autopsy in app/routes/api/so.py:54-239, mounted at /api/v1/va in app/routes/api/__init__.py:87) enforces no route-specific request.content_length limit and no type or maximum character-length check on the remark field (line 98). Requests are bounded only by Flask's global Config.MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH (default 2 MiB in config.py:137, configurable via the MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH environment variable, behind nginx client_max_body_size 55m in deploy/ingress-routes.conf:7). Note that public-demo accounts on PUB01 cannot reach this sink because app/services/public_demo_service.py:453-454,469-470 enforces social_autopsy_enabled=False and reviewer_social_autopsy_enabled=False, which app/routes/api/so.py:88-95 rejects with 403 forbidden. However, any authenticated coder, coding_tester, reviewer, or admin holding an active coding or reviewing allocation on a project with Social Autopsy enabled can store ~2 MiB strings (or up to MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH if raised in deployment) in VaSocialAutopsyAnalysis.va_saa_remark (sa.Text, app/models/va_social_autopsy_analysis.py:43), which are then echoed in the save response (app/routes/api/so.py:238), serialized in GET /api/v1/va/<va_sid>/workspace (app/routes/api/va_case.py:508,754), rendered into HTML in GET /vaform/<va_sid>/social_autopsy (app/services/case_content_service.py:559-561; app/routes/va_form.py:625), and projected into the mv_submission_analytics materialized view (app/services/submission_analytics_mv.py:945,1125).
claimed_root_cause: save_social_autopsy in app/routes/api/so.py:54-239 parses the JSON request body up to the global Config.MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH (default 2 MiB in config.py:137) without a route-level request.content_length cap and writes (data.get('remark') or '').strip() directly to VaSocialAutopsyAnalysis.va_saa_remark (sa.Text) at lines 98, 179, and 196 without verifying isinstance(..., str) or enforcing a character-length bound.

trace.description: POST /api/v1/va/<va_sid>/social-autopsy calls request.get_json(force=True, silent=True) without a route-specific request.content_length check, relying only on global Config.MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH (2 MiB default in config.py:137).
Extracts remark = (data.get('remark') or '').strip() or None without checking isinstance(remark, str), rejecting NUL bytes, or bounding character length.
Assigns the unbounded remark string to analysis.va_saa_remark on an existing active VaSocialAutopsyAnalysis row (or passes va_saa_remark=remark to a new VaSocialAutopsyAnalysis instance at line 196).

Commits the unbounded remark to VaSocialAutopsyAnalysis.va_saa_remark (sa.Text) in PostgreSQL and returns it in the JSON response at line 238, from where it is also read by workspace (app/routes/api/va_case.py:508), renderpartial (app/services/case_content_service.py:559), and mv_submission_analytics (app/services/submission_analytics_mv.py:945,1125).

evidence.description: save_social_autopsy parses JSON via request.get_json(force=True, silent=True) without checking request.content_length.
remark = (data.get('remark') or '').strip() or None has no character-length cap or string type check.
va_saa_remark is declared as an unbounded sa.Text column.
Config.MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH defaults to 2 * 1024 * 1024 (2 MiB) unless overridden by the MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH environment variable.
Comparable baseline put_note enforces _NOTE_BODY_CAP = 64 * 1024 (line 941) and _NOTE_MAX_CHARS = 20_000 (line 955).
Comparable baseline finalize enforces _FREE_TEXT_CAP = 4000 characters on coder final remark (line 611).
_social_autopsy_json loads row.va_saa_remark into the GET /api/v1/va/<va_sid>/workspace response (line 754).
mv_submission_analytics materializes saa.va_saa_remark AS social_autopsy_remark across active submissions.

blockers: OS-enforced sandbox execution is unavailable on this VM (predeclared promotion allowlist is empty), preventing local runtime reproduction of the oversized remark save and subsequent workspace/analytics read.

Production and staging environment values for MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH (config.py:137, default 2 MiB behind nginx client_max_body_size 55m in deploy/ingress-routes.conf:7) are outside repository source observation.

validation_plan.local: In an isolated test database, create a project with social_autopsy_enabled=True, allocate a test submission to a dummy coder, and send a POST request to /api/v1/va/<va_sid>/social-autopsy with valid selected_options for all three delay levels and a 500,000-character remark string. Verify that HTTP 200 is returned with the 500,000-character remark persisted in va_social_autopsy_analyses.va_saa_remark and returned by GET /api/v1/va/<va_sid>/workspace?mode=coding.
validation_plan.deployment: Inspect the deployed environment configuration (without sending large payloads to shared services) to confirm whether MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH is left at the 2 MiB default in config.py:137 or overridden to a higher value, and enforce a route-level Content-Length cap (e.g., 64 KiB) and character limit (e.g., 4,000 characters) in app/routes/api/so.py.

title: Data Management user update endpoint allows a project or site Data Manager to overwrite coding languages and profile fields of users shared with other projects
description: In `app/routes/data_management.py`, `PUT /data-management/api/users/<target_user_id>` (`manage_update_user`, `lines 1083-1180`) and `POST /data-management/api/users/<target_user_id>/resend-verification` (`manage_resend_verification`, `lines 974-1000`) authorize mutations on `target_user` via `_dm_can_manage_user_profile(target_user)` (`lines 1045-1081`). Unlike the comparable roster profile-edit baseline `mobile_sign_in_service.may_edit_account` / `_roster_rule` (`app/services/mobile_sign_in_service.py:155-194`, `231-259`, enforced by `PATCH /admin/api/projects/<project_id>/people/<target_user_id>/profile` at `app/routes/admin_organization.py:1639-1640`), which requires that the target user hold no privileged grants, have every active grant within the caller's manageable scope, and have no `MapProjectMember` rows outside the caller's managed projects (`_outside_member`), `_dm_can_manage_user_profile` passes if: (1) `target_user.other.get('created_by_user_id') == str(current_user.user_id)` (`lines 1054-1056`) regardless of current grants in other projects; (2) the target user satisfies `_managed_user_condition()` (`lines 187-194`, `1057-1065`), an existential check requiring only at least one active grant in `_listed_grants_condition()`; or (3) the caller is a wide writer (`_is_wide_writer()`, `lines 179-184`) and the target user has zero active grants and is not in `mentors.member_user_ids` (`lines 1066-1080`), without checking `MapProjectMember` outside the caller's projects. Consequently, a Data Manager in Project A (either for an already-shared user or after unilaterally granting a Project B user a role in Project A via `POST /data-management/api/access-grants`) can overwrite `target_user.job_title` (`line 1119`) and `target_user.vacode_language` (`line 1164`), disrupting coding/review language filtering (`app/decorators/va_validate_permissions.py:187`, `app/services/coder_workflow_service.py:112`, `app/services/reviewer_coding_service.py:403`) for Project B.
claimed_root_cause: `app/routes/data_management.py:_dm_can_manage_user_profile` (`lines 1045-1081`) uses creator attribution (`lines 1054-1056`), an existential single-grant check `_managed_user_condition()` (`lines 187-194`, `1057-1065`), and an unplaced-user check omitting `_outside_member` (`lines 1066-1080`), instead of requiring that all active grants (with none privileged) and all `MapProjectMember` memberships of `target_user` fall within the caller's manageable scope.

trace.description: PUT /data-management/api/users/<target_user_id> accepts JSON payload with job_title and/or languages from a caller with role data_manager or admin.
Checks _dm_can_manage_user_profile(target_user) before allowing job_title or languages updates.
Authorizes profile mutation if target_user matches _managed_user_condition() (or was created by current_user at line 1055, or has no active grants when caller is a wide writer at lines 1066-1080).
Subquery requires only that target_user has at least one active grant matching _listed_grants_condition(), ignoring active grants or MapProjectMember rows in other projects.
Overwrites target_user.vacode_language (and target_user.job_title at line 1119) and commits at line 1168, altering global account state across all projects.

evidence.description: _dm_can_manage_user_profile allows mutation when created_by_user_id matches (line 1055), when at least one active grant is managed via _managed_user_condition() (lines 1057-1065), or when the user has no active grants and caller is a wide writer (lines 1066-1080).
_managed_user_condition checks VaUsers.user_id.in_(select(VaUserAccessGrants.user_id)...) for any single active grant in _listed_grants_condition().
manage_update_user mutates target_user.job_title (line 1119) and target_user.vacode_language (line 1164) and commits (line 1168).

Comparable baseline _roster_rule / editable_user_ids (lines 155-194, 231-259) requires every active grant of the target user to be managed by the actor (none privileged) and no MapProjectMember row outside the actor's managed projects (_outside_member).
Roster profile endpoint enforces mobile.may_edit_account(current_user, user.user_id, project_id) and rejects shared accounts with 403.

blockers: OS-enforced sandbox execution with no external network, empty allowlisted environment, read-only target/tools, and scratch-only writes is unavailable on this VM, preventing dynamic execution of the Flask test client to record an observed result.

validation_plan.local: Run pytest inside the approved isolated test container against a dedicated test database (e.g., TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgresql://minerva:minerva@minerva_db_service:5432/minerva_test_verifier) with a test that creates User U holding an active coder grant in Project A (with vacode_language=['english', 'hindi']) and an active coder grant in Project B, authenticates as Project A's Data Manager (who has no grants in Project B), sends PUT /data-management/api/users/<U.user_id> with {'languages': ['english'], 'job_title': 'Changed'} and X-CSRFToken, and verifies whether 200 is returned and U.vacode_language is overwritten globally.

title: Project PIs and Data Managers can import existing Mentoring Institute admins into a project roster to issue one-time sign-in codes or overwrite their global profiles
description: Mentoring-institute staff and institute administrators are stored in `MapMentorInstituteUser` (`app/models/mas_mentor_institute.py:71-100`), where `is_admin=True` grants `mentor_institute_admin` authority (`app/models/va_users.py:326-330`, `app/decorators/role_required.py:83`) over `/admin/api/mentor-institutes/<code>/staff` (`app/routes/admin_mentor_institute.py:92-191`) without creating a `VaUserAccessGrants` row. While `app/routes/data_management.py:1080` explicitly checks `mentors.member_user_ids` to prevent Data Managers from editing unassigned mentoring-institute accounts, both `app/services/project_user_import_service.py` (`prepare_members` at lines 645-755) and `app/services/mobile_sign_in_service.py` (`may_issue_code`, `_roster_rule`, `issuable_user_ids`, `editable_user_ids`, `_outside_member`, and `may_issue_code_from_data_management` at lines 118-319) completely omit `MapMentorInstituteUser`. Consequently, a `project_pi` or project-scope `data_manager` of any organization-mode project can import a `mentor_institute_admin` (or mentoring-institute staff member) into `MapProjectMember` via `POST /admin/api/projects/<project_id>/users-grid/members/import`, issue a one-time 8-character sign-in code via `POST /admin/api/projects/<project_id>/users-grid/<target_user_id>/sign-in-code` for an unverified or mobile-only `mentor_institute_admin` and redeem it at `POST /valogin/code` or `POST /api/v1/auth/sign-in-code/redeem` to reset their password and take over their account, or overwrite a verified `mentor_institute_admin`'s global profile (`name`, `year_of_birth`, `sex`, `vacode_language`) via `PATCH /admin/api/projects/<project_id>/users-grid/<target_user_id>/profile`.
claimed_root_cause: `app/services/mobile_sign_in_service.py` (`may_issue_code`, `_roster_rule`, `issuable_user_ids`, `editable_user_ids`, `_outside_member`, `may_issue_code_from_data_management`) and `app/services/project_user_import_service.py` (`prepare_members`) check only `VaUserAccessGrants` and `MapProjectMember` for outside membership or privileged roles, ignoring active `MapMentorInstituteUser` memberships and `MapMentorInstituteUser.is_admin`.

trace.description: Accepts a CSV or XLSX upload at POST /admin/api/projects/<project_id>/users-grid/members/import from a project_pi or project-scope data_manager and calls user_import.prepare_members at line 1782.
Matches an existing active VaUsers account by email or mobile_login and marks it action='add_existing' without checking whether the user is in MapMentorInstituteUser or is a mentor_institute_admin.
Inserts MapProjectMember(project_id=project_id, user_id=user.user_id, added_by_user_id=actor_user_id), placing the mentoring-institute admin or staff account onto project_id's roster.

Evaluates on_project_roster(project_id, user_id_col), sa.not_(_outside_member(user_id_col, managed_projects)), and sa.or_(rule_a, rule_b). Because MapMentorInstituteUser is neither a VaUserAccessGrants row nor checked by _outside_member (line 262), an unplaced or in-project-granted mentor_institute_admin satisfies _roster_rule.

Permits a non-admin project_pi or project-scope data_manager to issue a sign-in code for any account satisfying _roster_rule that has no live phone session and no verified email; editable_user_ids (line 231) permits editing any active account satisfying _roster_rule regardless of email verification.

Calls mobile_sign_in_service.issue_code and returns the plaintext 8-character sign-in code for the target mentor_institute_admin (redeemable at POST /valogin/code or POST /api/v1/auth/sign-in-code/redeem to overwrite the user's password), while admin_project_user_panel_profile (line 1639) allows overwriting global profile fields via may_edit_account.

evidence.description: MapMentorInstituteUser stores mentoring-institute staff memberships and the is_admin flag (line 92) outside VaUserAccessGrants and MapProjectMember.

mentor_institute_create_staff and mentor_institute_remove_staff (line 166) are gated by @role_required('admin', 'mentor_institute_admin'), granting institute admins authority to create and remove institute staff.
_dm_can_manage_user_profile explicitly checks target_user.user_id not in mentors.member_user_ids([target_user.user_id]) to block Data Managers from managing unassigned mentoring-institute accounts.
prepare_members matches existing active users by email or mobile and adds them to MapProjectMember without checking mentors.member_user_ids.
_outside_member checks only MapProjectMember for memberships outside the actor's managed projects, omitting active MapMentorInstituteUser memberships.

validation_plan.local: In an isolated test database, create an active organization-mode project P1 with a project_pi (or project-scope data_manager) actor, and an active MasMentorInstitute M1 with an active MapMentorInstituteUser(is_admin=True) user U1 (both unverified-email/mobile-only and verified-email variants). title: Unconsented Cross-Project Member Import Triggers _outside_member Lockout on Victim Project Account Management and Sign-In Code Issuance
description: A project_pi or project-scope data_manager in Project B can upload any existing active Project A user's email address or 10-digit mobile number to POST /admin/api/projects/<project_B>/users-grid/members/import with dry_run=0. Because prepare_members() and apply_members() in app/services/project_user_import_service.py:645-791 attach any matched active VaUsers account to MapProjectMember for Project B without checking whether the user already holds active grants, worker placements, or membership in another project, this unilaterally creates a MapProjectMember row in Project B. Downstream, _outside_member() in app/services/mobile_sign_in_service.py:262-269 evaluates to True whenever any MapProjectMember row exists outside the caller's managed projects. Because _roster_rule() (app/services/mobile_sign_in_service.py:155-194) and may_issue_code_from_data_management() (lines 293-312) enforce sa.not_(_outside_member(...)) across all non-admin callers even when the user holds active grants exclusively in Project A, Project A's project_pi and data_manager are immediately locked out of editing the user's profile (403 Forbidden on PATCH /admin/api/projects/<project_A>/users-grid/<user_id>/profile), sending password-reset links (403 Forbidden on POST /admin/api/projects/<project_A>/users-grid/<user_id>/password-reset), and issuing one-time sign-in codes from both the project roster (404 Not Found on POST /admin/api/projects/<project_A>/users-grid/<user_id>/sign-in-code) and the data-management panel (404 Not Found on POST /data-management/api/users/<user_id>/sign-in-code). Project A's managers cannot remove the MapProjectMember row in Project B to recover management of their own worker.
claimed_root_cause: prepare_members() and apply_members() in app/services/project_user_import_service.py:645-791 allow any project_pi or project-scope data_manager to attach any active existing VaUsers account to their project's MapProjectMember table by email or canonical 10-digit mobile number without verifying whether the account already belongs to or holds active grants/worker rows in another project, while _outside_member() in app/services/mobile_sign_in_service.py:262-269 treats any MapProjectMember row in an unmanaged project as disqualifying in _roster_rule() and may_issue_code_from_data_management() even when the target holds active grants only in the victim manager's project.

trace.description: Accepts multipart CSV/XLSX uploads at POST /admin/api/projects/<project_id>/users-grid/members/import from any admin, project_pi, or project-scope data_manager of an active organization-mode project (_guard(project_id, roster=True) at line 1765).

Matches uploaded email or 10-digit mobile rows against all VaUsers globally (lines 678-691) and marks any active existing user not yet in MapProjectMember for project_id as action='add_existing' (line 744) without checking existing memberships, grants, or workers in other projects.
Inserts MapProjectMember(project_id=project_id, user_id=user.user_id, added_by_user_id=actor_user_id) for every add_existing row when dry_run=0.
Returns True via SQL EXISTS when the target user has any MapProjectMember row with project_id outside the caller's managed project_ids.

Requires sa.not_(_outside_member(user_id_col, managed_projects)) for both grant-holding (rule_a) and unplaced (rule_b) roster users, causing issuable_user_ids (line 218) and editable_user_ids (line 248) / may_edit_account (line 256) to exclude the victim user for Project A's non-admin managers.

Rejects Project A's project_pi and data_manager with 403 Forbidden on profile edits (line 1640) and password-reset requests (line 1698), while sign-in code issuance is rejected with 404 Not Found on both the roster endpoint (line 1448) and data-management endpoint (app/routes/data_management.py:1020).

evidence.description: prepare_members() assigns action='add_existing' to any matched active VaUsers account not already in the caller's project MapProjectMember set, regardless of whether the user holds active grants, worker placements, or membership in another project.
apply_members() writes MapProjectMember(project_id=project_id, user_id=user.user_id, added_by_user_id=actor_user_id) without requiring target consent or checking cross-project affiliation.

_roster_rule() Conjoins sa.not_(_outside_member(user_id_col, managed_projects)) above sa.or_(rule_a, rule_b), so an unplaced MapProjectMember row in Project B overrides active grants held exclusively in Project A (rule_a).

may_issue_code_from_data_management() enforces not db.session.scalar(sa.select(_outside_or_signed_in(target_user_id, projects))), blocking Project A data managers from issuing sign-in codes on /data-management/api/users/<id>/sign-in-code once Project B adds a MapProjectMember row.

admin_project_user_panel_profile() and admin_project_user_panel_password_reset() (line 1698) return 403 Forbidden ('This account is shared with other projects; only an admin may change/reset it.') when may_edit_account() is False, and admin_project_users_grid_sign_in_code() (line 1448) returns 404 Not Found when may_issue_code_in_project() is False.

title: Unconsented Cross-Project Roster Attachment via Imports Discloses Full Account Profile, Unqueried Contact Channel, Devices, and Global Security Event Log
description: A project_pi or project-scope data_manager can unilaterally attach any active user on the platform (including platform admins, PIs of other projects, and mentoring-institute scientists) to their project roster without target consent or admin approval via two import paths: (1) uploading a single-channel (email-only or mobile-only) CSV/XLSX to POST /admin/api/projects/<project_id>/users-grid/members/import (prepare_members and apply_members in app/services/project_user_import_service.py:645-791), which inserts a MapProjectMember row, or (2) a project_pi uploading a workers sheet to POST /admin/api/organization/<project_id>/import (_import_workers in app/services/organization_service.py:2598-2663), which passes user_email directly to create_worker/update_worker -> resolve_user (accepting either a user_id UUID from masked search results or an email address at lines 1831-1833) while omitting the require_on_project_roster guard enforced on POST/PATCH /admin/api/organization/<project_id>/workers (app/routes/admin_organization.py:755, 860). Once attached to MapProjectMember or MasOrgUnitWorker, on_project_roster (app/services/organization_service.py:3956-3970) evaluates to True for that user in the attacker's project. This unlocks GET /admin/api/projects/<project_id>/users-grid/<target_user_id> (admin_project_user_panel at app/routes/admin_organization.py:1558-1603) and GET /admin/api/projects/<project_id>/users-grid (get_project_users_grid at app/services/organization_service.py:4490-4530), disclosing the target user's unqueried or previously masked contact channel (bypassing lookup_existing_user at organization_service.py:3116-3118 and _dm_user_json masking at app/routes/data_management.py:224-233), demographics (year_of_birth, age, sex), all live enrolled mobile devices across all projects via list_account_devices (bypassing the all-grants coverage check in _device_management_user at app/services/user_directory_service.py:488-520), and up to 100 global AuthSecurityEvent records across all projects including cross-project actor names (_panel_activity at app/routes/admin_organization.py:1521-1541).
claimed_root_cause: _import_workers (app/services/organization_service.py:2598-2663) omits require_on_project_roster and allows resolving arbitrary active users by UUID or email via resolve_user (lines 1816-1838), while prepare_members/apply_members (app/services/project_user_import_service.py:645-791) allows a project_pi or project-scope data_manager to attach any active platform account to MapProjectMember using a single identifier; subsequently, admin_project_user_panel (app/routes/admin_organization.py:1558-1603) gates full contact disclosure, cross-project device inventory (list_account_devices), and unfiltered global security event history (_panel_activity at lines 1521-1541) solely on on_project_roster (app/services/organization_service.py:3956-3970) rather than requiring exclusive account management (may_edit_account / _device_management_user) or scoping security events to the project.

trace.description: Accepts a multipart CSV/XLSX upload from a project_pi or project-scope data_manager on POST /admin/api/projects/<project_id>/users-grid/members/import (or via admin_org_import at line 1123 on POST /admin/api/organization/<project_id>/import).

Matches any active VaUsers account globally by email alone or mobile_login alone when the other field is left blank in the uploaded row (lines 715-729), marking the row action as add_existing (line 744) without checking whether the target is a platform admin or belongs to other projects.

Inserts a MapProjectMember(project_id=project_id, user_id=user.user_id) row for the matched user (or _import_workers at app/services/organization_service.py:2640 inserts a MasOrgUnitWorker row linked via resolve_user by UUID or email without calling require_on_project_roster).
Evaluates to True whenever the target user exists in MapProjectMember or MasOrgUnitWorker for project_id (lines 3967-3969), satisfying _roster_person (app/routes/admin_organization.py:1482).

Returns the target user's full email and phone, year_of_birth, age, sex, all live devices across all projects via list_account_devices(user.user_id) (line 1576), and unfiltered global AuthSecurityEvent history with actor names via _panel_activity (lines 1521-1541, 1591).

evidence.description: prepare_members resolves user = by_email or by_mobile and only rejects mismatches when both email and mobile are supplied on the row, allowing attachment of any active account knowing only one channel.

_import_workers calls create_worker and update_worker (line 2630) with user=row.get('user_email'), which calls resolve_user (lines 1816-1838) accepting a user_id UUID or email without enforcing require_on_project_roster (unlike admin_org_create_worker at app/routes/admin_organization.py:755 and admin_org_update_worker at line 860).

lookup_existing_user explicitly withholds the unqueried contact channel from non-admin callers, and _dm_user_json (app/routes/data_management.py:224-233) masks email and phone for out-of-reach users, both of which are bypassed once the user is attached to the roster.

_device_management_user requires a non-admin data manager to cover every live native-device-role grant on the target user across all projects before calling list_account_devices, whereas admin_project_user_panel (app/routes/admin_organization.py:1576) calls list_account_devices unconditionally for any user on the project roster.
_panel_activity queries AuthSecurityEvent by E.user_id == user_id across all projects without a project filter or exclusive-management check, joining VaUsers on actor_user_id to return actor.name.

Authenticate as a project_pi or project-scope data_manager of PROJ_A, upload a 1-row CSV containing only the target's email (or upload a workers CSV with the target's user_id UUID in user_email to POST /admin/api/organization/PROJ_A/import with dry_run=0), and then request GET /admin/api/projects/PROJ_A/users-grid/<target_user_id> to observe the target's unqueried mobile number, demographics, PROJ_B device metadata, and PROJ_B security event log with actor names.

title: Non-admin managers can issue on-screen Sign-In QR tokens for verified-email, live-phone, and cross-project accounts to take over device sessions and evict active phones
description: POST /api/v1/users/<user_id>/sign-in-qr (app/routes/api/users.py:151-166) delegates authorization and token issuance to app/services/sign_in_qr_service.py:issue (lines 176-237) and may_issue (lines 118-130). Unlike 8-character mobile sign-in codes in app/services/mobile_sign_in_service.py (may_issue_code at lines 118-152, issuable_user_ids at lines 197-228, and may_issue_code_from_data_management at lines 293-312), sign_in_qr_service omits three anti-takeover guards required by docs/policy/mobile-sign-in.md sections 3 and 8 (lines 186-210 and 418-425): (1) issue() allows delivery='show' for non-admin callers (project_pi, data_manager, and unit site_pi In-charge) even when user.email_verified is True, returning the plaintext token ('code': token) in the HTTP response (lines 232-237) instead of restricting on-screen QR delivery for verified-email accounts to admins or email-only delivery; (2) may_issue() never checks _live_phone(user_id), allowing a non-admin manager to issue and redeem a QR token at POST /api/v1/auth/sign-in-qr/redeem (app/routes/api/auth.py:277-316 -> app/services/sign_in_qr_service.py:305-372) to open an authenticated device bearer session as a collector who is already signed in on a phone and even decommission their active phone via replace_device_id (line 350 -> device_auth_service.check_device_slot at lines 726-789); (3) may_issue() ignores MapProjectMember (_outside_member), allowing a data manager who looks up an unplaced member of another project via GET /data-management/api/users/lookup and grants them a collector role via POST /data-management/api/access-grants to immediately issue and redeem a Sign-In QR for that account.
claimed_root_cause: app/services/sign_in_qr_service.py:may_issue (lines 118-130) and issue (lines 176-237) check only whether the target user is eligible for a collector project and holds at least one active grant with no active grant outside authz.grant_list_filter(actor, _grants=grants), omitting the non-admin delivery='show' restriction for verified-email accounts, the sa.not_(_live_phone(user_id)) guard, and the sa.not_(_outside_member(user_id, projects)) guard enforced in app/services/mobile_sign_in_service.py.

trace.description: POST /api/v1/users/<user_id>/sign-in-qr accepts delivery ('show' by default) from any authenticated admin, project_pi, or data_manager (including unit site_pi) and calls sign_in_qr.issue at line 161.

may_issue(actor, user_id) checks only that the target has at least one active grant and no active grant outside authz.grant_list_filter(actor, _grants=grants), without checking verified email, _live_phone, or _outside_member.

issue(actor, user_id, delivery) verifies may_issue and eligible_project, checks user.email_verified only when delivery == 'email' (line 191), and returns the raw Sign-In QR token ('code': token) in the HTTP response when delivery == 'show' (lines 232-237).
POST /api/v1/auth/sign-in-qr/redeem accepts the raw token and optional replace_device_id without prior authentication and calls sign_in_qr.redeem at line 295.

redeem() calls devices.check_device_slot(user, replace_device_id=replace_device_id) (which can decommission an active phone at the 3-device cap) and then enrols a new device (line 362) and opens an authenticated device bearer session for the target user (line 367).

evidence.description: may_issue() checks only active grants against authz.grant_list_filter(actor) and omits _live_phone, _outside_member, and verified-email checks.

issue() enforces user.email_verified only when delivery == 'email', permitting non-admin callers to use delivery == 'show' on verified-email collector accounts and receive the plaintext token at line 233.
Baseline comparison: may_issue_code() explicitly blocks non-admin code issuance when the target user has a verified email (sa.not_(verified_email)).

Baseline comparison: may_issue_code_from_data_management() enforces _outside_or_signed_in(target_user_id, projects) at line 312 to block non-admin issuance when the target belongs to an outside project or has a live phone session.
Policy section 8 specifies that Sign-In QR is emailed only to a verified email address or shown on screen once to an admin, and that an account without a verified email gets the on-screen delivery.

validation_plan.local: Run pytest inside an isolated test database (TEST_DATABASE_URL) with a test that authenticates as a non-admin project_pi or data_manager, creates or selects an active interviewer with email_verified=True, an active AuthDeviceSession (live phone), or a MapProjectMember row in another project, posts {'delivery': 'show'} to POST /api/v1/users/<user_id>/sign-in-qr, Assert HTTP 201 with a 'code' token, and posts that token to POST /api/v1/auth/sign-in-qr/redeem (including with replace_device_id at the 3-phone cap) to observe session issuance and device decommissioning.

title: training_report_service._reviewer_session_ids omits MasTrainingSession.status == 'active', allowing reviewer_data_manager participants of closed legacy sessions to access trainer reports and CSV exports
description: When an administrator closes a training session via close_training_session (app/services/training_demo_service.py:2337-2340), _set_session_status (lines 2308-2335) sets MasTrainingSession.status = 'closed' and deactivates the session participants' VaUserAccessGrants while keeping MapTrainingParticipant.status = 'active' so that reopen_training_session (lines 2343-2346) can restore grants for non-removed participants. Every other participant authorization query in app/services/training_demo_service.py (has_pending_onboarding at line 2368, participations at line 2385, may_use_area at line 2445, self_coding_units_select at line 2478, standard_set_sids at line 2517, and complete_onboarding at line 2548) explicitly filters on MasTrainingSession.status == 'active'. However, _reviewer_session_ids(viewer_id) in app/services/training_report_service.py:84-100 filters MasTrainingSession only on MasTrainingSession.session_type.is_(None) (line 93) and MapTrainingParticipant.status == 'active' (line 97), omitting MasTrainingSession.status == 'active'. Because the routes in app/routes/dm_training.py:36-63 enforce @role_required('data_manager', 'reviewer', 'admin') via effective_roles(user) (app/decorators/role_required.py:61-75, app/services/authz/predicates.py:687-722), a non-admin user whose TRN01 reviewer grant was deactivated on session close—but who holds an active reviewer, data_manager, site_pi, or project_pi grant in any other project or another active training session—passes the route gate and is authorized by authorized_session (app/services/training_report_service.py:103-125) and sessions_for_viewer (lines 128-136) to view and export the closed legacy session's trainee names, emails, and ICD-10 reference answer keys via /data-management/training/<ref>, /data-management/training/<ref>/coders.csv, and /data-management/training/<ref>/cases.csv.
claimed_root_cause: app/services/training_report_service.py:_reviewer_session_ids (lines 84-100) selects legacy session IDs with MasTrainingSession.session_type.is_(None) (line 93) and checks MapTrainingParticipant.status == 'active' (line 97) without requiring MasTrainingSession.status == 'active', even though closing a session sets MasTrainingSession.status = 'closed' while leaving MapTrainingParticipant.status = 'active'.

trace.description: GET /data-management/training/<ref> (along with /training at line 38, /training/<ref>/coders.csv at line 54, and /training/<ref>/cases.csv at line 61) accepts a session reference from a user holding any active data_manager, reviewer, or admin effective role and calls _report(ref).
_report(ref) delegates session authorization and report generation to report_service.training_session_report(ref, current_user._get_current_object()).
training_session_report calls authorized_session(session_ref, viewer) to verify whether the viewer may read the requested session's trainer report.

_reviewer_session_ids filters MasTrainingSession only on MasTrainingSession.session_type.is_(None) and MapTrainingParticipant.status == 'active' (line 97), omitting MasTrainingSession.status == 'active'.
authorized_session permits any non-admin viewer whose MasTrainingSession.training_session_id is in _reviewer_session_ids(viewer.user_id), without checking MasTrainingSession.status == 'active'.
training_session_report returns the closed session's trainee names, contact emails/masked phones, coding statistics, and source ICD-10 reference causes for HTML rendering and CSV export.

evidence.description: legacy = sa.select(MasTrainingSession.training_session_id).where(MasTrainingSession.session_type.is_(None)) omits MasTrainingSession.status == 'active' in _reviewer_session_ids.
authorized_session checks MasTrainingSession.training_session_id.in_(_reviewer_session_ids(viewer.user_id)) without filtering on MasTrainingSession.status == 'active'.
sessions_for_viewer filters list_training_sessions() against _reviewer_session_ids(viewer.user_id), keeping closed legacy sessions visible to former reviewer_data_manager participants.
_set_session_status sets row.status = status ('closed') and deactivates VaUserAccessGrants for active participants while leaving MapTrainingParticipant.status == 'active'.
Comparable training authorization gate may_use_area explicitly requires both MapTrainingParticipant.status == 'active' and MasTrainingSession.status == 'active'.
@role_required('data_manager', 'reviewer', 'admin') gates the trainer report routes using global effective_roles(user) rather than a session-scoped active grant check.

Policy states that only an administrator and a user with an active reviewer_data_manager participation in that same session may read the trainer report, while line 194 states that closing a session deactivates every participant's training grants.

Owner policy confirmation is needed on whether docs/policy/training-demo-project.md ('Trainer report', lines 386-399) intends for a legacy session's reviewer_data_manager participant to lose trainer report access when the session is closed via close_training_session (matching the MasTrainingSession.status == 'active' filter enforced in training_demo_service.py).

title: Revoked or closed-session trainees and interviewers retain closed-session draft, post-submission revision, and cross-scope read access via owner-only VaWebIntakeDraft checks
description: While docs/policy/web-intake.md (lines 89-93, digitva-9xn9.22) intentionally allows an interviewer whose real-project grant was removed to finish an in-flight browser draft (status == 'draft'), two source-verified authorization gaps in app/services/web_intake_service.py exceed that baseline because draft and submission helpers authorize via draft.user_id == user.user_id without verifying an active grant or active training session on (draft.project_id, draft.site_id, draft.org_unit_id). First, for training sessions (docs/policy/training-demo-project.md lines 194-197, 212), remove_participant (app/services/training_demo_service.py:2297) and close_training_session (line 2337 via _set_session_status at line 2324) deactivate the participant's VaUserAccessGrants while leaving the session's MasOrgUnit.is_active == True. When a trainee removed from or after closure of session S001 remains enrolled in another active session S002, training_scope.resolve('interview') (app/services/training_scope.py:61-84) and @role_required('interviewer') pass via S002, and list_drafts (app/services/web_intake_service.py:1853-1859), get_draft (lines 1862-1875), save_draft_sections (lines 2367-2474), and submit_draft (lines 2829-3063) only check draft.user_id == user.user_id, training_scope.keeps_project(draft.project_id) (True across all TRN01 sessions), and _require_live_org_unit(draft) (lines 2644-2680, True because MasOrgUnit.is_active remains True), allowing the trainee to read, edit, and submit drafts into closed/revoked session S001. Second, once an interview is already submitted (status == 'submitted', outside the in-flight draft exemption), find_own_submission (app/services/web_intake_service.py:3090-3096) checks only VaWebIntakeDraft.va_sid == va_sid, VaWebIntakeDraft.user_id == user.user_id, and VaWebIntakeDraft.status == 'submitted', omitting both _require_scope and training_scope.keeps_project.
